MAJOR: gate2_completion_check._docs_only() re-implements the docs-only predicate (fnmatch + hardcoded skip-globs default) instead of calling gate_predicates.is_docs_only; set_status/gate_decisions use the shared one. Two copies can diverge — direct violation of the "single predicate" acceptance criterion and the stated purpose of gate_predicates.py.

core/backlog.py (shipped control-plane) loads scripts/dev/gate_decisions.py by raw filesystem path via importlib on every Gate 2 check, re-exec'ing the module per call. A deployed core without scripts/dev breaks all completions (fail-closed GATE_ERROR, i.e., availability outage), and the "keeps core free of dev imports" claim is only cosmetically true — this is a runtime dependency on dev tooling layout, not an architectural boundary.

The ordering predicate (decision.at >= evidence.at) is silently skipped when the evidence record lacks a parseable `at`, and _ingest writes `at` as naive local time while decisions are UTC; _parse_ts assumes naive==UTC. Both cases can let a pre-evidence approval pass as valid, weakening the STALE_APPROVAL guarantee.

store-registry.json declares gate-baseline.json owner as "core/gate_predicates.py", but the module actually lives at scripts/dev/gate_predicates.py. Registry drift misroutes ownership/impact analysis for a fail-closed gate config.

force path in set_status bypasses record_gate_decision entirely, hardcodes by="hil:forced" (not a real actor, though it passes the hil: prefix check), and performs two non-atomic updates (append decision, then set status). No fsync/rollback semantics if the second write fails.
MINOR: The negative self-test matrix required by the AC (missing Gate 1, stale approval, force-without-PF_GATE_FORCE, pending diff findings) is split inconsistently: gate1_transition_check has --self-test but it is never wired into precheck/ci-cd-gates, so the gate-1 predicate matrix never executes in CI.

The hardcoded skip-globs default ["docs/**","**/*.md","config/**"] is duplicated in gate2_completion_check, gate_decisions, and gate_predicates call sites; a config change to size_gate.skip_globs silently changes Gate 2 semantics with no versioned contract.

record_gate_decision for gate 2 does not validate that the recorded decision.at is after the evidence timestamp at write time; ordering is only enforced at read, so an out-of-order decision can be persisted and later confuse audit history.
set_status does not handle a missing item (get_epic returns {}); if the working set happens to be docs-only, a nonexistent eid can pass the Gate 2 predicate before update() no-ops.

Observability: all gate outcomes are plain print() to stdout with no structured event/JSON line in the enforcement path (--report exists but CI runs are grep-driven); long-term, machine consumers will parse free text.

gate_decide.py exists as the canonical recorder but core.backlog.record_gate_decision re-exports the same path with sys.modules[__name__] injection — two entry points to the same operation invites drift.
NIT: gate1_transition_check imports gate_predicates as gp at module level and re-imports it inside _self_test, shadowing the outer binding.
gate_predicates.is_docs_only imports fnmatch inside the function body on every call.
gate2_completion_check.py imports fnmatch at top level but never uses it directly (only _docs_only does).
SUMMARY: Sound overall design: shared predicates, fail-closed defaults, baseline governance, and append-only decision journal are the right shape, and the self-test/unit matrices cover the key negative cases.

Top risks: the "single predicate" AC is violated by _docs_only duplication; shipped core/backlog.py reaching into scripts/dev via importlib is a fragile boundary with availability consequences; and the decision/evidence ordering check is bypassable due to missing/naive `at` timestamps.
Recommend fixing the docs-only duplication, making the ordering check fail-closed on missing `at`, and moving gate_predicates into a real core module before this is treated as a hard enterprise gate.
